subject: Volume pegging & burst management — commercial proposal and operational playbook
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Volume pegging & burst management — commercial proposal and operational playbook

Hi Jane / CloverMed team,

Thanks again for the time last week — attached is a compact commercial proposal and an operational playbook that maps pricing behavior to realistic traffic profiles we discussed. I highlighted the sections you flagged in the RFP (token rate tiers, overage smoothing, invoice true-up cadence and SLA-credit mechanics). Attachments: 20270531-volume-pegging-model.xlsx, Service-Playbook-v1.pdf.

High-level summary (see attached workbook for worked scenarios):
- Base commit: 50M tokens / month (year 1) at $0.00110 per token for text-generation models; embeddings billed at $0.00045 per vector unit.
- Volume peg: commit anchored to an annualized baseline with a quarterly onramp window (first 90 days can climb to 150% of monthly commit without overage charges).
- Surge buffer: a 10% monthly surge pool (prepaid at a 25% discounted rate vs on-demand) that absorbs short spikes; once consumed, overages bill at 1.25x base unit rate with smoothing rules (see below).
- True-up / smoothing: 3-month rolling average true-up with a 5% graceband before credits apply; invoices show both raw usage and smoothed-basis adjustments.
- Pilot concession: first two months — waived overage on up to 20% of usage above commit, and one-time onboarding credit of $10,000.
- SLA credits and operational fallback: per-route latency SLOs listed in the playbook; fallback to compatible lower-cost model variant if capacity constraints trigger (automated routing).

Questions for you so we can finalize pricing language for the SOW:
1) Do you prefer the surge buffer to be prepaid as a named pool on the invoice, or billed monthly as a line item as consumed?
2) Any preference on true-up cadence (we propose quarterly with 3-month rolling smoothing)?

If it helps, I can run two worked examples for your current forecast (the workbook has an example profile but I can load your month-by-month forecast into it). Can we set a 30-minute follow-up tomorrow to review the workbook?

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Volume pegging & burst management — commercial proposal and operational playbook

Jane — thanks, great questions. I’ve attached a short worked invoice and a text explanation (sample_invoice_example.pdf). Short answers inline below and the invoice walks through a 70% spike example.

- Invoice example: the invoice has three sections: 1) Base commit charge, 2) Surge buffer (prepaid pool consumption & remaining balance), 3) Overages & smoothing adjustments. For a 70% spike in a single month with a 10% prepaid surge pool: the prepaid pool covers the first 10% of the spike; the remaining 60% is tallied, then our 3-month rolling average is computed. If the rolling-average-based overage for that month exceeds the 5% graceband, the invoice shows a provisional overage, plus a smoothing credit that phases across the next two billing periods. The net effect is smaller month-to-month billing volatility. See example: Month A raw overage = 60% -> billed over month A at 75% of on-demand rate; smoothing credit applied over month B/C at negotiated smoothing factor.

- Surge buffer roll-forward: by default surge pools do not auto-roll beyond the calendar month (they’re designed to provide short-term absorption). If you prefer carry-forward, we can price a rolling surge pool (charged at a slightly higher prepaid rate) that carries up to 3 months; pricing worksheet has both options and a toggle. Please indicate which you'd prefer on the SOW.

- Security contact: Marissa Cole (cc’d) is our lead for compliance and will connect you with our Security & Privacy SME for Private deployment questions (audit logs, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2 artifacts).

Worked example (short):
- Baseline commit: 50M tokens (charged at $55,000/month).
- Prepaid surge pool (10%): 5M tokens (charged upfront at $0.000825/token = $4,125).
- Month with 85M raw usage (70% spike):
  - Prepaid surge covers first 5M (no overage).
  - Remaining raw overage = 30M tokens.
  - Apply 3-month rolling smoothing: provisional overage recognized as 20M for billing this month (smoothing factor example), billed at 1.25x base unit rate = $0.001375/token -> provisional charge $27,500.
  - Smoothing credit applied over next 2 invoices to reconcile to actual overage.

I’ve uploaded the worked invoice and a copy of the workbook with toggles to the Drive link below so you can flip the smoothing options and see live numbers: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3Cexample-drive-link

Next steps: I’ll schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow with Marissa, Ben and our Pricing ops lead to walk through the workbook if that works for you.

Cheers,
Rachel

Attachments: sample_invoice_example.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

Hi Jane / team — looping in to cover compliance handoff and to propose a modest commercial concession to accelerate the pilot sign. Two items from our side: 

1) Pilot concession proposal (we can bake into the SOW):
   - Month 0–1: waive overage on the first 20% above commit (in addition to the prepaid surge pool).
   - Month 2: 50% discount on overages between 20–50% above commit.
   - Purpose: reduces friction for traffic discovery and gives you burst visibility without immediate cost shock.

2) Onramp discount ladder for Year 1 (if you convert to an annual commit within 90 days):
   - Convert within 90 days: additional 7% on committed spend for the first year.
   - Convert within 180 days: additional 4% on committed spend.

We’ll hand Security/Privacy off to our SME — Ben, can you please share the SOC2 artifact package and the contact details for the Private deployment SME? I’ll prepare the SOW language for the pilot concession and the onramp ladder.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
